meaning: "O Tārā, I pray, O Tārā, O swift one, so be it." A call to Tara, the female buddha who comes quickly to those in fear or danger.
purpose: To call on Tara for protection and the courage to act.
when: In fear or difficulty, or as a morning practice.
note: Tara is honoured across Tibetan and Himalayan Buddhism, and her name is shared with the Hindu Mahavidya Tara, a different figure in a different tradition.
source: Tibetan Buddhist practice; translation as given in the Wikipedia article on Tara
name: Green Tara Mantra
pronunciation: AUM taa-ray tut-taa-ray tu-ray svaa-haa; in Tibetan practice AUM is said short, ta-ray tu-ta-ray tu-ray so-ha
